flags.headline: -6.45% to $307.17 -- AI-infra-capex repricing, 2nd session, directly matches key_risk
flags.detail: Lam Research fell 6.45% alongside a broader chip-equipment/test-and-measurement selloff. Driver: renewed scrutiny of AI-infrastructure capex sustainability after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's own framing this week of compute overbuild as an existential/bankruptcy risk if revenue doesn't scale to match reserved data-center capacity -- language that has spooked the whole AI-capex-dependent equipment complex rather than reflecting anything company-specific to LRCX. Applied Materials and Teradyne also down 4-5% on the same news. Second consecutive session of AI-infra-capex-driven weakness in this cohort (CRDO/MRVL flagged AMBER yesterday); today LRCX and KEYS join with clearer, tier-1-sourced attribution and explicit thesis-language matches, which is why this escalates to RED rather than repeating yesterday's single AMBER macro cap.
flags.thesis_link: Matches LRCX key_risk: 'Forward P/E of 36.55x and 248% stock price appreciation over 52 weeks reflect AI-driven demand assumptions -- any deceleration in AI infrastructure spending or fab construction delays could trigger significant multiple compression.'

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance (Applied Materials/Lam Research/Teradyne selloff on AI-capex repricing)

flags.headline: Aug-31 wildfire-reform deadline 11 days out, still no draft legislation -- CEO reiterates credit-downgrade warning
flags.detail: No resolution to the core risk: California's legislative session ends Aug 31 (11 days out) with still no draft wildfire-liability-reform legislation. CEO Pedro Pizarro reiterated that insufficient action in 2026 would likely trigger credit-rating downgrades for SCE and peer California investor-owned utilities, pushing SCE's already-lowest-investment-grade S&P rating toward junk and raising customer financing costs. Shares calm (-0.37% to $73.39) -- this remains a catalyst-timing RED, not a price-action RED.

California's complex regulatory and political environment creates uncertainty around cost recovery, rate base returns, and wildfire liability frameworks.'
